SELECT cls, boat, COUNT(*) trips, SUM(anglers) anglers, SUM(yt) yt, ROUND(SUM(yt)/SUM(anglers),3) rate
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 6 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 91 AND 121
GROUP BY cls, boat
HAVING SUM(anglers) > 30
ORDER BY rate DESC
LIMIT 20

SELECT cls, COUNT(*) trips, SUM(anglers) anglers, SUM(yt) yt, ROUND(SUM(yt)/SUM(anglers),3) rate
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 6 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 106 AND 121
GROUP BY cls
ORDER BY rate DESC

SELECT
  fish_date_season AS season,
  CASE WHEN fish_date_doy < 152 THEN 'spring(<152)'
       WHEN fish_date_doy < 244 THEN 'summer(152-243)'
       WHEN fish_date_doy < 305 THEN 'fall(244-304)'
       ELSE 'late(305+)' END AS bucket,
  cls, COUNT(*) trips, SUM(anglers) anglers, SUM(yt) yt, ROUND(SUM(yt)/SUM(anglers),3) rate
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season < 6 AND cls IN ('day_1_5','overnight','three_quarter')
GROUP BY season, bucket, cls
HAVING SUM(anglers) > 20
ORDER BY bucket, cls, season

SELECT avail_season AS season, avail_doy AS doy, value AS oni
FROM climate
WHERE index_id = 'oni' AND avail_season = 6
ORDER BY avail_doy DESC
LIMIT 5

# SEASON 6 — PLANNING TURN AT DAY 121, 21:00. Budget $800/2000, PTO 8/10, season_score 11.77 (rank 7/34).

## STATUS: THE BOOKING BUG IS RESOLVED — DO NOT RE-LITIGATE
Day-91 notes worried nightly decisions weren't firing (91 straight nights, zero bookings). That's
over. Since day 91 the nightly self booked **8 trips, all THREE_QUARTER, all settled**: shares of
1.61, 1.07, 0.80, 1.10, 1.40, 0.31, **4.81(!)**, 0.68 — sum 11.77, season rank 7 of 34, ahead of
most of the field. $1200 spent, 2 PTO used (both committed: d114, d133). The reasons attached to
each booking show real trailing-rate reasoning (best-sampled hot boat vs dead HD), matching the
day-91 plan almost exactly. **Keep doing exactly this — book 3Q on the best-sampled hot boat every
night it's offered, no hesitation.**
One loose end: `journal.md` still shows **zero Season 6 entries** (all S02 stale lines from an old
season). Bookings prove the decision call IS running and IS acting — so this is at most a
journal-writing quirk, not the structural bug feared at day 91. Not worth spending a tool call on
again; just note it if it's still true next planning turn.

## Data check at day 121 (confirms the bite is still on, well past noise)
Last 30 days (doy 91-121), by boat (>30 anglers only), season 6:
- **three_quarter San Diego: 1.623 (29 trips, 1247 anglers) — still the anchor, huge sample.**
- three_quarter Mission Belle: 1.557 (28 trips, 702 anglers) — essentially tied with San Diego.
- three_quarter Malihini: 1.474 (17 trips, 502 anglers) — solid third.
- three_quarter Daiwa Pacific 1.484 (6/155), Fisherman III 1.227 (3/75), Mustang 1.128 (5/47) —
  smaller samples, fine as bonus picks if the top three aren't scheduled.
- day_1_5 Invicta 3.098 (2/41), overnight Prowler 1.237 (3/59) — thin but positive, watch these grow.
- **HD_AM/HD_PM still dead: 0.004 and 0.014 over 30 days.** Structural zero, confirmed every check
  this season. Never force an HD booking "just to book something."
Last 15 days (doy 106-121) pooled by class: three_quarter 1.676 (50 trips/1438 anglers, still the
best-sampled positive read), day_1_5 1.573 (n=4, thin), overnight 0.74 (n=6, thin), multi_day (1.5-day)
3.614 (n=3, very thin but very hot — watch this class as more boats get scheduled).

## Context: this looks like a genuinely hot (El Niño-leaning) season, not a fluke
ONI this season: 0.70 (d9), 0.80 (d40), 0.73 (d71), 0.65 (d99) — mild-to-moderate El Niño, holding
steady, not fading. Pooled history (seasons 1-5) shows **spring 3Q rates are normally 0.07-0.53** —
season 6's actual spring 3Q rate (1.6-1.7) is far above every prior season's spring baseline. This
is a strong signal, not noise.
Pooled fall (doy 244-304) history splits by apparent ENSO state: seasons 3 & 4 (warmer years) show
day_1_5 1.88-3.62 and overnight 1.56-2.29 in fall — both classes clearly beating 3Q. Seasons 1, 2, 5
(cooler/negative years) stayed weak in fall for those classes (day_1_5 0.31-0.91, overnight 0.29-0.49).
**Given positive ONI now, lean toward expecting day_1_5/overnight to climb through summer into a
good fall window — but confirm with actual trailing rates as they arrive, don't assume on ENSO alone.**

## Budget and PTO pacing (day 121 → season end ~day 330, ~209 days left)
- $800 left, 8 PTO left. Current 3Q trade ($150, ~1.6 yt/angler) is already outperforming most
  historical fall peaks — **keep booking it every night it's offered on San Diego / Mission Belle /
  Malihini (priority in that order by current rate), no-PTO weekend/holiday dates first**, same as
  the day-91 rule. Don't let cash sit idle waiting for a hypothetical better window; this bite is
  live now.
- Reserve **~$400-500** for Aug-Nov, to switch into day_1_5 ($550) or overnight ($400) once their
  trailing rate clearly and repeatably beats 3Q's (watch for day_1_5/overnight rates crossing above
  ~1.6-1.8 on decent sample, not just a 1-2 trip spike). Pooled data above says this is plausible in
  a warm year like this one.
- PTO: 8/10 left, only 2 used so far (both worthwhile — one of them produced the 4.81 share). PTO
  caps at 10 and never carries over, so don't hoard it defensively — commit PTO (14-day lead) for a
  weekday slot on San Diego/Mission Belle/Malihini when no no-PTO date is available and the boat is
  clearly hot, same bar as any other booking decision.

## Self-check for next planning turn (read this section FIRST)
- Re-pull the same 30-day/15-day boat table — check San Diego/Mission Belle/Malihini stayed on top,
  re-rank if a new boat has taken over.
- Check whether day_1_5/overnight trailing rates have grown past 3Q's — if either clears ~1.8-2.0
  on a real sample (>5 trips, >100 anglers), start shifting bookings there per the reserved budget.
- Recheck HD stayed dead (it always has) and recheck ONI trend (rising/falling from ~0.7).
- Confirm bookings have continued at roughly the same pace since day 121 (no new dormancy bug) and
  check if journal.md ever picked up real S06 entries.
